- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

One conversion, in `local/host-page-adaptation`. Nothing under `.claudinite/shared/` was touched.

## The rule converted

From `host-page-adaptation/RULES.md`, "Never trust a write — verify by re-reading":

> …aim your events at a node **inside the app's own subtree** — the selected element if it has focus, otherwise a known app node. A modern app delegates key handling near its root, which is a descendant of ``, so an event dispatched at `document` or `body` bubbles *past* it and is never seen.

It clears the skill's first gate (it governs how we drive a host page, not what this product renders), it is always-testable (the receiver at a `dispatchEvent` site is a static signature), and no existing check covered it: the sibling `synthetic-input-events-bubble` judges whether the event **can** travel, never **where** it is aimed. Both can be satisfied and the write still fail — `document.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown', { bubbles: true }))` bubbles perfectly, past nothing.

## The check

`input-events-target-app-subtree`, **blocking**, in `local/host-page-adaptation`.

Fires when a real-input event (the `INPUT_EVENT_CLASSES` set, resolved through one constructor-alias hop and one local-variable hop, exactly as the sibling resolves it) is dispatched at a receiver written out **literally** as `document`, `document.body`, `document.documentElement`, or `window`/`globalThis`/`self` (optionally qualified, e.g. `window.document.body`).

Parsed, not grepped, and quiet in the deliberate direction:

- a target the code **resolves** — the `activeElement ?? cell ?? body` ladder a real adapter picks with — is beyond a static read, so the rule says nothing. That is why this repo's own `page-adapter/writer.js` is quiet: the mistake the rule is after is *aiming* at a global, not *falling back* to one.
- `CustomEvent` (your own signal to your own listener) and non-input events (`new Event('resize')`, which is exactly what `window` is the right target for) are never judged.
- comments are stripped first, so prose describing the trap cannot fire it.

## See-it-fail

Red-first fixtures in `pack.test.mjs`: five firing cases (`document`, `document.body`, documentElement/window/qualified, the variable hop, the aliased `fire()` helper), six quiet ones (app node, resolved-target ladder, `CustomEvent` at window, `new Event('resize')`, an unreadable local, a comment, test scaffolding), the naive-grep case proving the parsing is *necessary*, and the corpus case over the real `extension/src/`.

Neutering the rule's `run` to return `[]` fails **exactly** the five firing tests and nothing else — verified live in this run, then reverted.

## Deletion test — the prose stays whole

Applied to the paragraph the check now stands beside: it **stays**, untrimmed. It carries a second rule the check does not cover (poll the re-read — the host renders asynchronously, so the DOM right after your event is the DOM *before* the app processed it) and the value the check cannot judge (which node to aim at *instead*). Per the skill, prose is deleted whole or not at all — never trimmed — so the paragraph keeps its text and gains a pointer to the check for the half now mechanized, in the pack's established style. `README.md`'s check table and enforcement column are updated to match.

## Also in the diff

`assignedTo` moves from `synthetic-input-events-bubble.mjs` into `lib.mjs` — both dispatch-site rules now resolve the same one-variable hop, and the existing fixtures cover that path.

## About the re-proposal

This exact conversion was opened once before as #165 (2026-08-09) and closed unmerged three days later with no comment recorded — the tracker issue (#83) has no entry explaining a rejection. Rather than guess at an undisclosed reason, I re-derived the candidate independently against current `RULES.md` (unchanged since #165's base) and re-confirmed it's still the strongest, only remaining candidate: `browser-speech`'s backlog has been re-derived as exhausted across five independent sweeps (07-30, 08-01 through 08-05), and `host-page-adaptation` has no other always-testable rule left unconverted per the 08-09 sweep's rule-by-rule verdict. If this is closed again, a one-line reason on #83 would save the next sweep from re-proposing it a third time.

## Green

`npm ci && npm test` — 452 tests, 21 files, all passing (up from the 438-test baseline on `main`). `npm run trace` — 111/111 Active requirements covered, no phantom IDs.

{"number":207,"title":"Claudinite: convert the dispatch-target rule to a check","body":"Weekly **prose-to-checks** sweep over `.claudinite/local/packs` (tracking issue #83, work item #199). One conversion, in `local/host-page-adaptation`. Nothing under `.claudinite/shared/` was touched.

## The rule converted

From `host-page-adaptation/RULES.md`, "Never trust a write — verify by re-reading":

> …aim your events at a node **inside the app's own subtree** — the selected element if it has focus, otherwise a known app node. A modern app delegates key handling near its root, which is a descendant of ``, so an event dispatched at `document` or `body` bubbles *past* it and is never seen.

It clears the skill's first gate (it governs how we drive a host page, not what this product renders), it is always-testable (the receiver at a `dispatchEvent` site is a static signature), and no existing check covered it: the sibling `synthetic-input-events-bubble` judges whether the event **can** travel, never **where** it is aimed. Both can be satisfied and the write still fail — `document.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown', { bubbles: true }))` bubbles perfectly, past nothing.

## The check

`input-events-target-app-subtree`, **blocking**, in `local/host-page-adaptation`.

Fires when a real-input event (the `INPUT_EVENT_CLASSES` set, resolved through one constructor-alias hop and one local-variable hop, exactly as the sibling resolves it) is dispatched at a receiver written out **literally** as `document`, `document.body`, `document.documentElement`, or `window`/`globalThis`/`self` (optionally qualified, e.g. `window.document.body`).

Parsed, not grepped, and quiet in the deliberate direction:

- a target the code **resolves** — the `activeElement ?? cell ?? body` ladder a real adapter picks with — is beyond a static read, so the rule says nothing. That is why this repo's own `page-adapter/writer.js` is quiet: the mistake the rule is after is *aiming* at a global, not *falling back* to one.
- `CustomEvent` (your own signal to your own listener) and non-input events (`new Event('resize')`, which is exactly what `window` is the right target for) are never judged.
- comments are stripped first, so prose describing the trap cannot fire it.

## See-it-fail

Red-first fixtures in `pack.test.mjs`: five firing cases (`document`, `document.body`, documentElement/window/qualified, the variable hop, the aliased `fire()` helper), six quiet ones (app node, resolved-target ladder, `CustomEvent` at window, `new Event('resize')`, an unreadable local, a comment, test scaffolding), the naive-grep case proving the parsing is *necessary*, and the corpus case over the real `extension/src/`.

Neutering the rule's `run` to return `[]` fails **exactly** the five firing tests and nothing else — verified live in this run, then reverted.

## Deletion test — the prose stays whole

Applied to the paragraph the check now stands beside: it **stays**, untrimmed. It carries a second rule the check does not cover (poll the re-read — the host renders asynchronously, so the DOM right after your event is the DOM *before* the app processed it) and the value the check cannot judge (which node to aim at *instead*). Per the skill, prose is deleted whole or not at all — never trimmed — so the paragraph keeps its text and gains a pointer to the check for the half now mechanized, in the pack's established style. `README.md`'s check table and enforcement column are updated to match.

## Also in the diff

`assignedTo` moves from `synthetic-input-events-bubble.mjs` into `lib.mjs` — both dispatch-site rules now resolve the same one-variable hop, and the existing fixtures cover that path.

## About the re-proposal

This exact conversion was opened once before as #165 (2026-08-09) and closed unmerged three days later with no comment recorded — the tracker issue (#83) has no entry explaining a rejection. Rather than guess at an undisclosed reason, I re-derived the candidate independently against current `RULES.md` (unchanged since #165's base) and re-confirmed it's still the strongest, only remaining candidate: `browser-speech`'s backlog has been re-derived as exhausted across five independent sweeps (07-30, 08-01 through 08-05), and `host-page-adaptation` has no other always-testable rule left unconverted per the 08-09 sweep's rule-by-rule verdict. If this is closed again, a one-line reason on #83 would save the next sweep from re-proposing it a third time.

## Green

`npm ci && npm test` — 452 tests, 21 files, all passing (up from the 438-test baseline on `main`). `npm run trace` — 111/111 Active requirements covered, no phantom IDs.
